To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have evaluated the zero-field-splitting interactions for the single-ion Ni(II) center in a Zn3Ni single-crystal doped complex, and we have related this to the zfs interaction in the Ni4 molecule of the SMM by irreducible tensor theory.

the single-ion zfm parameters for the Ni(II) center in the doped single-molecule magnet [Zn3Ni(hmp)(4)(dmb)(4)Cl(4)] were measured by high-frequency electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy and that the easy axes of magnetization associated the single-ion zero field interaction are tilted away from the crystal axis.

high-field EPR measurements on a single crystal of a doped single-molecule magnet allowed us to evaluate the zero-field-splitting parameters associated with the single Ni(II)-ion in the complex, and these parameters are then used to evaluate the zero field interaction of the S = 8 ground state of the Ni4 molecule.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new class of SMMs that exhibit slow relaxation of magnetization at low temperatures and high magnetic fields, which is of great interest in the field of molecular nanomagnets.
the study of single-ion zero-field interactions in single-molecule magnets.
a new class of single molecule magnets (SMM) based on Ni(II) ions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the single-ion zfS interactions in complex 1 are responsible for the fast QM of the SMM in complex 2.
the single-ion zfS parameters for the Ni(II) ions in complex 2 are responsible for the fast Q TM observed for this molecule.
the fast QTM in complex 2 is due to a single-ion zfs interaction tilted away from the easy axis of magnetization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fast QTM in 2 is caused by the single-ion zfss and the inclination of the easy axes away from the molecular c axis.
the fast QTM in complex 2 is a consequence of the tilted zfs axes and not a consequence of a low D value.
the single-ion zfss in the Ni(II) ions in 1 and 2 are not large enough to prevent QTM.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the single-ion zfm parameters can be evaluated by high-field EPR for a SMM with a single magnetic ion.
the single-ion zfS interactions are not negligible and should be included when calculating the zfs parameters of SMMs from single-crystal high-field electron parametric resonance spectra.
single-ion zfs interaction is the main source of anisotropy in SMMs, and the single-ion zfS parameters are the key to understanding the magnetic properties of these molecules.
